business_model.claim: HCSG sells management and operating services for the housekeeping, laundry, linen, maintenance and dietary departments of healthcare and senior-living facilities across the United States, serving more than 2,700 facilities.
quotes: We provide management, administrative and operating expertise and services to housekeeping, laundry, linen, facility maintenance and dietary service departments within nursing homes, retirement complexes, rehabilitation centers, hospitals and campuses located throughout the United States.

business_model.claim: The company reports two segments, Environmental Services (EVS) and Dietary. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, EVS was about 45.2% of revenue ($638.7 million) and Dietary about 54.8% ($774.5 million).
quotes: We are organized into two reportable segments: housekeeping, laundry, linen and other services (“Environmental Services” or “EVS”) and dietary department services (“Dietary”).

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors and MD&A.
business_model.claim: Customers are mainly long-term and post-acute care providers whose revenue depends on Medicare, Medicaid and other third-party payers. Changes in reimbursement therefore affect their ability to pay HCSG.
quotes: Many of our customers rely on reimbursement from Medicare, Medicaid and other third-party payers.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the 10-K risk factors.
business_model.claim: Revenue comes from service agreements that either party can cancel on short notice, so revenue depends on winning and keeping facilities rather than on long locked-in terms.
quotes: Our agreements with customers typically provide for a renewable service term cancellable by either party upon 30 to 90 days’ notice after an initial period of 60 to 120 days.

business_model.claim: Management names new customers and additional services to existing customers as the primary revenue drivers. Third-quarter 2026 revenue rose 3.3% to $479.6 million, which the company attributes to client wins and retention, price increases and pass-through costs.
quotes: We believe the primary revenue drivers of our business are our ability to obtain new customers and to provide additional services to existing customers.
The increase in revenues was driven by client wins and retention, contractual price increases and pass-through costs to customers.

business_model.claim: Labor is the largest cost, especially in EVS, where labor was about 78.3% of segment revenue in 2025, compared with 58.8% in Dietary.
quotes: EVS labor costs accounted for approximately 78.3% of EVS revenues in 2025 while Dietary labor costs accounted for approximately 58.8% of Dietary revenues in 2025.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A and risk factors, and in the 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Dietary has a heavy supplies cost, with food supplies about 30.9% of Dietary revenue in 2025. This makes Dietary margins sensitive to commodity food prices.
quotes: In contrast, food supplies consumed in performing our Dietary services accounted for approximately 30.9% of Dietary revenues.

business_model.claim: The company can contractually pass through union and minimum-wage increases, but not all wage inflation, so cost pass-through can lag or be incomplete and compress margins.
quotes: Although we have contractual rights to pass union and minimum wage increases through to our customers, we do not have a contractual right to automatically pass through all wage rate increases resulting from wage rate inflation or local job market adjustments, and we may be delayed in doing so.

business_model.basis: Stated in the company's earnings release.
business_model.claim: Segment margins differ: third-quarter 2026 segment margin was 13.3% for EVS on $217.2 million of revenue and 8.7% for Dietary on $262.4 million.
quotes: Segment revenues and margins for Environmental and Dietary Services were reported at $217.2 million and 13.3% and $262.4 million and 8.7%, respectively.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K, the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release.
business_model.claim: Customer credit losses are a major swing cost. Bad debt provisions were $83.1 million in 2025, including Genesis bankruptcy-related expense, and a $6.1 million Genesis benefit was recorded in the third quarter of 2026.
quotes: we have recorded bad debt provisions (in an Allowance for Doubtful Accounts) of $83.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2025

During the three months ended September 30, 2026, we recognized a $6.1 million benefit in bad debt expense related to the reassessment of the current expected credit loss from the 2025 Genesis bankruptcy.

business_model.claim: Genesis Healthcare, which filed for Chapter 11 in July 2025, was a large single customer, at 7.3% of 2025 consolidated revenues.
quotes: Genesis contributed 7.3%, 8.7% and 10.9% of our total consolidated revenues for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors and the 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Self-insurance for general liability and workers' compensation adds a cost that depends on claims experience. Loss-estimate updates reduced third-quarter 2026 costs of services by $1.8 million, versus $3.1 million a year earlier.
quotes: We carry high deductible general liability, workers’ compensation and other insurance programs and therefore retain a substantial portion of the risk associated with the possible losses under such programs.
updates to our loss estimates for workers’ compensation and general liability reduced costs of services provided by $1.8 million and $3.1 million, respectively.

business_model.claim: A single distributor handles most food and dining supplies, which concentrates supply-chain exposure.
quotes: one distributor distributed more than 50% of our food and non-food dining supplies

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q income statement and cash flow statement.
business_model.claim: Reported profitability on the income statement: for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, revenues were 1,413,178 against cost of services of 1,182,161 and SG&A of 143,034, giving net income of 73,633 (all figures in thousands of dollars). The same period of 2025 had net income of only 27,815.
Management's cost framework is a cost-of-services goal of about 86% of revenue and an SG&A goal of 9.5% to 10.5%. Third-quarter cost of services was 83.2% of revenue.
quotes: The Company’s goal is to manage cost of services in the 86% range.
The Company’s goal is to manage SG&A in the 9.5% to 10.5% range, with the longer-term goal of managing those costs into the 8.5% to 9.5% range.

business_model.claim: Besides services, HCSG earns investment and other income from cash, notes and marketable securities and from deferred compensation plan assets. This was $2.1 million in the third quarter of 2026 versus $11.8 million a year earlier, when it included ERC-related interest income.

is expected to contribute over $150 million in annual revenue at comparable margins to the Company’s while being immediately accretive to earnings
